hook: The owl that catches your rat is dying from it.
caption:
The owl that catches your rat is dying from it.

Owls are perfect ambush predators because their feathers are serrated to break up the air over their wings, so the wingbeat is silent in the frequency range a mouse can hear, and their facial disk funnels sound to ear openings placed asymmetrically on the skull, allowing them to pinpoint prey under snow or leaf litter by sound alone. Then they eat the rodent. Across North America, second-generation anticoagulant rodenticides used in homes and commercial pest control accumulate in the rodents the owls hunt, and the owl bleeds out internally over weeks. A 2020 survey of barred owls passing through California wildlife rehabilitation centers found anticoagulant residues in over eighty percent of carcasses tested. The poison sold to kill the mouse is killing the owl that would have eaten it for free.
